sentence: This project builds a computer tool that uses deep learning to find tumor buds and sort risk in colorectal carcinoma.
This project runs a shared lab that offers imaging and recording tools to watch brain activity in behaving animals during addiction.
This project studies whether tunneling nanotubes help HIV replicate and spread in the placenta and pass from mother to fetus.
This project looks at contaminants that cause infections or toxic harm in animals and animal food, using a One Health approach.
This project refines a wearable near-infrared spectral tomography system to test whether changes in tumor vasculature predict early response to chemotherapy in breast cancer.
This project studies RNA in blood after stroke to build a machine learning tool that predicts stroke outcomes.
This project studies how blocking a signaling pathway of vasoactive intestinal peptide can wake the immune system to attack pancreatic cancer.
This project builds a system that uses endoscopic ultrasound to assess pancreatic tissue in a measured, objective way for pancreatic cancer screening.
This project engineers a molecule to trigger broadly neutralizing antibodies against HIV in an outbred animal model, as a blueprint for vaccine design.
This project tests a violence prevention program that uses community health advocates and legal aid to protect youth from community violence.
This project provides computer tools and data services that help diabetes researchers make sense of omics and health record data.
This project tests whether gene-engineered T cells that target B lymphocytes can teach the body to accept transplanted kidneys in non-human primates.
This project runs an imaging facility that provides equipment for viewing cells, tissues and organs, including small animal imaging.
This project builds vaccines given at mucosal surfaces to protect against human noroviruses, using vaccine vector platforms.
This project maintains a resource of olive baboons free of adventitious viruses for scientists studying vaccines, transplantation and Alzheimer's disease.
This project tests whether a gas sensor made from olfactory neurons can detect endometriosis from exhaled breath, using cell cultures, organoids and mice.
This project looks for targets and imaging methods that can guide cancer therapies, including for breast cancer and bladder cancer.
This project studies how a blood test that finds genetic changes in cell-free DNA can help patients with advanced pancreatic cancer.
This project tries to find genetic factors that make patients more likely to develop long-lasting pain after surgery.
This project studies how senescent T cells affect immune responses in aging and HIV, and how senolytic drugs might reduce them.
